subject: Brightlane: data usage commitments, residency & exclusion from model updates
message_1_subject: Brightlane: data usage commitments, residency & exclusion from model updates
message_1_body:
Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion with you and Marco. Per the call, I wanted to recap the specific privacy and data-handling controls Brightlane requested and the steps Redwood will take to lock those into the procurement process. I’ve copied Rafael (security) and Monica (eng) who will own the technical and contract items.

Summary of Brightlane asks (as I captured them):
- No customer content used for model training or model improvements at any time (including offline fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or data-plane telemetry feeding internal training sets).
- EU residency for any persisted request/response logs for your production traffic.
- Short-term operational logging for debugging (we discussed 30 days), with pseudonymization for PII fields and an option for you to request additional redaction.
- Appendix / DPA language and a simple contract addendum confirming the model-learning exclusion and data residency.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) I’m attaching a draft DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) that includes a dedicated clause excluding Brightlane data from any model learning.
2) Rafael will provide SOC 2 artifacts and a short description of our pseudonymization pipeline by EOD tomorrow.
3) Monica will outline the log retention and redaction config we’ll apply in the Brightlane prod tenant (defaults: 30 days, can extend to 0 days on request).
4) We’ll prepare a short addendum (one paragraph) to append to the MSA that explicitly prohibits training-on-customer-data without a signed, opt-in amendment from Brightlane.

Can you confirm the above captures the asks accurately? If so, we’ll push the DPA + addendum to your legal contact and schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk through technical configs.

Thanks,

—David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(d) +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (draft), SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf
message_2_subject: Re: Brightlane: data usage commitments, residency & exclusion from model updates
message_2_body:
Thanks David — that looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: Brightlane requires a standing prohibition on using any customer content for training (we do not want our logs, prompts, or generated outputs used to improve models). This must be explicit in the DPA/addendum.
- Residency: All persisted logs for production traffic must remain in the EU (we can provide region/project IDs for the Cloud provider).
- Logging: 30 days is fine as a default for now; we need a simple API/portal control to purge logs early and an SLA to confirm purge execution.
- PII handling: Any fields we mark as PII must be pseudonymized before being stored; where pseudonymization is not feasible we need clear deletion steps and evidence of deletion on request.

Please route the DPA + addendum to legal@brightlane.com. If you can include a short paragraph we can sign that confirms: (a) no training without express opt-in amendment, (b) logs retained in EU, and (c) operational logs retained for a configurable period with default 30 days.

We’ll aim to review once you send the updated DPA. Please include pointers to the SOC 2 documents and a contact for purge requests.

—Ellen
VP Product, Brightlane Health
message_3_cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Brightlane Legal <legal@brightlane.com>
message_3_subject: Re: Brightlane: data usage commitments, residency & exclusion from model updates — evidence and next steps
message_3_body:
Hi Ellen / legal team,

Following David’s recap and Ellen’s confirmation, quick technical & evidence notes from our side: 

1) DPA/addendum: David attached Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf — we’ll insert a single-line addendum clause that states Brightlane data will not be used for model training, evaluation, benchmarking, or any model improvement activity unless Brightlane signs a separate written opt-in amendment. We’ll circulate the updated DPA to legal@brightlane.com by 2027-07-01 17:00 CET.

2) SOC2 & evidence: Attached SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf contains scope and the relevant control mappings for our data-handling processes. Full SOC 2 artifact access can be provided via a secure link on request; I’ll include that link in the DPA email.

3) Logging & retention: Our standard tenant configuration for enterprise customers supports region pinning. For Brightlane we’ll pin persisted logs to EU regions only. Operational logs used for live debugging are rotated to an encrypted object store and retained for 30 days by default. We support on-demand purge via an API endpoint and will provide a signed purge confirmation that includes a timestamp and a short proof file (hash + deletion job id).

4) PII pseudonymization: We will apply field-level pseudonymization rules (token replace + reversible mapping stored in a KMS-wrapped store only accessible by a restricted ops role). If you instruct us to avoid reversible mapping, we will instead apply irreversible hashing for those fields and document the approach.

5) Contract & procurement flow: After you confirm the wording you want for the addendum, we’ll push the DPA + addendum to DocuSign and copy your legal mailbox.

Action items: 
- David: send updated DPA + one-paragraph addendum to legal@brightlane.com (owner).
- Ellen/legal: confirm single-paragraph addendum language or propose edits.
- Brightlane: provide cloud region/project IDs if you want region pinning to a specific account (optional).

I’ll also add an internal ticket to the onboarding plan for the purge API + proof-of-deletion flow so we can include delivery dates in the mutual action plan.

Regards,

Rafael Mendes
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf
